title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention and timeouts
author: Ava Thompson
description:
Motivation: production workloads have observed unfair queueing under mixed latency profiles leading to token latency p99 regressions and intermittent starvation of small requests when long-running requests saturate GPU lanes. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve fairness, add bounded queueing/backpressure, and surface request-level timeouts to prevent starvation.

Summary of changes: - Introduce a dual-queue scheduler: short-path queue for low-token/count requests and long-path queue for high-cost requests. Requests are dynamically classified by estimated tokens and KV-cache hits. - Implement weighted dequeue policy with starvation prevention tokens: long-path dequeues yield capacity credits to short-path when short-path wait exceeds 50ms. - Add per-request enqueue timestamps and a max-queue-time TTL; requests exceeding TTL are failed fast with a clear error code and metrics emitted. - Extend scheduler config with tunables: short_queue_max, long_queue_max, fairness_alpha, starvation_threshold_ms, request_queue_ttl_ms, and enable_early_drop boolean. - Improve accounting to prefer requests with hot KV-cache hits; KV-cache-hit score reduces request cost for scheduling decisions. - Add adaptive backpressure: when GPU occupancy > 95% and queue depth high, scheduler reduces long-path admit rate via a token-bucket limiter. - Add extensive metrics and tracing: queue_length_{short,long}, queue_time_histogram, starvation_drops, fairness_score, kv_cache_hit_ratio, scheduler_decision.evts.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on rtx-a100 cluster with mixed workload (60% short 20-100 tokens, 40% long 800-2048 tokens) show: - tail latency (short requests) p99 reduced from 420ms to 210ms under sustained load. - overall throughput preserved within 3% of baseline. - starvation_drops introduced (configurable) to prevent unbounded queue growth; observed <0.1% failures under synthetic load, but prevented p99 amplification.

Testing and rollout: - unit tests for queueing logic and starvation edge cases added. - integration tests in perf-canary harness included; canary runs on a subset of capacity for 48h. - feature gated behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.fairness_v2 and config defaults tuned conservatively. - documented new config in docs/runbooks/continuous-batcher.md and added Linear links. - Rollout plan: enable on canary cluster for 48h, evaluate metrics, ramp 2x every 24h with abort criteria on p99 regressions >10% or increased error rate.

Related: ENG-3248 (scheduler fairness), ENG-3310 (kv-cache-aware scheduling), SUP-1123 (customer report of starvation in production).

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Nice approach. Two questions: 1) how do we choose fairness_alpha? 2) can early-drop be toggled per-tenant?
Ava Thompson: Answered: fairness_alpha default 0.6 chosen from grid search (see perf notes). Early-drop is a config flag and exposed per-tenant via runtime config in Dedicated/Private deployments.
Priya Nair: We need stronger unit tests around race between admission and KV-cache updates to avoid miscounts.
Ava Thompson: Added a deterministic unit test that simulates concurrent kv-cache population and admit; also added a comment in scheduler.rs explaining the ordering guarantees.
Samir Patel: CI failed first run due to flakiness in test_starvation; seems timeout was too tight. Re-ran and passed. Consider increasing test timeout to reduce flakes.
Ava Thompson: Increased test harness timeout and added retry in perf-canary job; documented in perf/benchmark notes.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler: reduced p99 for short requests via dual-queue fairness, added starvation prevention and request queue TTLs, KV-cache-aware admit scoring, and configurable tunables. Feature gated and rolled out via canary.
notes_for_oncall: If enabled on production, watch metrics: queue_length_short, queue_length_long, starvation_drops, short_request_p99, scheduler_decision.evts. Abort if short_request_p99 increases >10% or starvation_drops >0.5% for >30m.
